blocker.summary: The causal chain for the sub_821D6C20 SIGSEGV is resolved down to a specific internal failure exit inside sub_821CC508 (r443 established this is the function whose -1 return causes sub_821D5F48 to fail and skip constructing the renderer object at 0x82935D98; r442 established the caller treats that failure as non-fatal and proceeds regardless). r444 disassembled sub_821CC508 live (it's a large state machine, switch/goto-heavy per r443's earlier decompile) and found TWO distinct -1-return sites, not one -- live breakpoints on both plus the first GetLastError-equivalent call site showed only the SECOND site (+6171) actually fires; the first (+6046) and the error-check call never trigger. Immediate context at the taken site: ctx.r3 is set to a constant (0x8275a414), sub_821D4988 is called with it (its own return value is never checked), and the unconditional -1 return follows right after -- a 'log then fail' pattern matching sub_821F5B18's role for a different failure in r442. An attempt to read the string/data at guest address 0x8275a414 (as a diagnostic message) came back empty -- not yet resolved whether the address computation is off, the data isn't initialized yet at that point, or it isn't a string at all. Named for r445, two independent tracks: (1) decompile sub_821D4988 to understand its role and why the string read failed; (2) live-trace sub_821CC008 (already partly characterized by r441 as real file enumeration) to identify the specific file/path involved in whatever operation sub_821CC508 is polling. The native_vulkan_backend.cpp backlog commit decision (r433/r434/r438) remains the other open, user-dependent thread.
